name: Claude
tagline: An AI assistant to evaluate for writing, analysis, coding and document-based workflows.
description: Claude is an AI assistant for writing and analysis workflows; current plan details and independent ratings are not verified here.
pros: A controlled task set can compare output quality and editing effort against the team's current process.
Long-document or multi-step workflows can be evaluated using representative material.
A review rubric can expose factual errors and missing caveats before adoption.
A fixed task set can measure factual accuracy and editing effort.
A human-review rubric can expose uncertainty and unsupported output.
cons: Generated output can be wrong, incomplete or overconfident even when well written.
Data handling and retention terms should be checked before using confidential inputs.
Capabilities, limits and availability can change by model and plan.

content.title: Define the task and acceptance criteria
content.body: Select two or three real tasks, such as summarizing a policy, drafting a customer response or explaining a code change. Define the required facts, format, tone, citations and prohibited content before running the test. Use the same source material and time budget for every candidate.

content.title: Measure accuracy and editing effort
content.body: Record factual errors, missing requirements, unsupported claims, formatting failures and minutes needed to make the output usable. Include examples where the correct response is to state uncertainty or ask for missing information. Do not judge only fluency or length.

content.title: Context and repeatability
content.body: Test how the system handles long source material, follow-up instructions and conflicting details. Keep the prompt, input version and output together so another reviewer can reproduce the result. Re-test after material model or workflow changes.

content.title: Privacy and governance
content.body: Review current terms for uploaded content, retention, training use, access controls and enterprise administration. Do not submit secrets, regulated information or confidential client material unless the organization's policy and contract permit it. Define who reviews and approves outputs before external use.

content.title: Cost and rollout
content.body: Estimate seats or usage, integration work, review time and failure handling. Pilot with a bounded group and measure quality, adoption and cost against a baseline. Verify current model availability, usage limits and plan terms directly.

content.title: Pilot acceptance criteria
content.body: Build a small evaluation set from real tasks and include both routine and difficult examples. Have reviewers score correctness, completeness, source fidelity, tone and editing time using the same rubric. Keep the input and model output version so results can be compared after product changes.

content.title: Failure cases and human review
content.body: Include conflicting source passages, missing context, an ambiguous instruction and a question that cannot be answered from the provided material. Check whether the assistant preserves uncertainty rather than inventing a fact. Define which outputs need human approval before publication or action.

content.title: Decision record
content.body: Document approved use cases, prohibited data, prompt ownership, review rules, retention and the process for correcting errors. Estimate usage and review costs with realistic volume. Verify current product and plan terms directly and re-run the evaluation after significant model or workflow changes.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Claude?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Claude when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Test a representative task and verify current capabilities and limits directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: How should a team test Claude?
faqs.answer: Use the same real input, expected outcome and acceptance criteria each time. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown, including setup time, manual work and failure handling.

faqs.question: Which limitations should be checked in Claude?
faqs.answer: Check the exact plan, integrations, permissions, export, data retention, recovery and ongoing administration. Treat untested or undocumented capabilities as unknown until confirmed.

faqs.question: Are Claude prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, plan limits and independent ratings are not verified in this review. Check official documentation and obtain a dated quote before purchase.

faqs.question: What should be confirmed before adopting Claude?
faqs.answer: Confirm the core workflow, access controls, integrations, data export, account offboarding, support responsibilities and renewal terms. Assign an owner for the implementation and ongoing review.

author: Marcus Rivera
learningCurve: Minimal — most users can get started within an hour
whoShouldUse: Writers, analysts, developers, and teams can evaluate Claude for drafting, summarizing long material, exploring ideas, and assisting with code or document workflows. Use representative prompts and check factual accuracy, source traceability, context handling, and how well outputs fit the team's review process.
whoShouldNotUse: Do not treat Claude's responses as verified facts or use them as the sole basis for legal, medical, financial, security, or other high-impact decisions. Teams handling confidential information should review current data-use terms and controls, and should keep human review for outputs that affect customers or production systems.
